sentences.text: This creature possessed an elongated skull measuring 11 cm in length.
A bony crest widened toward the snout, reaching a height of 2 cm.
Its mouth contained heterodont teeth, meaning they had different shapes.
Scientists estimate the wingspan was approximately 120 cm.
Unlike other basal pterosaurs, it had a flexible tail without stiffening rod-like vertebral extensions.
Fossils were found in Late Triassic rocks in Austria dating to about 215 million years ago.
The genus was named in 2002 by Fabio Marco Dalla Vecchia and colleagues.
Analysis of tooth wear suggests the animal primarily ate hard invertebrates.
Later analyses placed it in the family Campylognathoididae related to Campylognathoides and Eudimorphodon.
It lived during the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, between 215.38 and 205.7 million years ago.
It is debated whether Austriadactylus is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Eudimorphodon.
